attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Refusal to eat or speak and difficulty breathing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He had a mild fever and sore throat yesterday but worsened rapidly overnight. Today, he developed high fever and has been drooling. His parents say he's sitting up and leaning forward, breathing through his mouth. They deny any cough.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of immunodeficiency disorders
- No family history of congenital airway abnormalities
- Maternal grandfather with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
He is febrile with a temperature of 39.4°C (103°F), heart rate of 140/min, and respiratory rate of 36/min. Oxygen saturation is 95% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears anxious and is sitting upright with his neck extended. His breathing is labored, and inspiratory stridor is audible. Examination of the oropharynx is deferred due to concern for airway instability.

Provider: Dr. Michael Okafor, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
High fever, difficulty swallowing, and hoarse voice

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department nine months after a previous admission for similar symptoms. He is brought by his parents due to a 6-hour history of high fever, difficulty swallowing, and a hoarse voice. His parents report that he has been drooling and seems to prefer sitting upright.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Acute bacterial epiglottitis with obstruction (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- No family history of immunodeficiency disorders
- No family history of congenital airway abnormalities
- Maternal grandfather with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

VITAL SIGNS:
He has a temperature of 39.2°C (102.6°F), heart rate of 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child appears anxious, has a muffled voice, and is sitting in the tripod position.
Examination of the throat is deferred to avoid potential airway compromise.

IMAGING:
A lateral neck x-ray is obtained and shows an enlarged epiglottis.

His parents report that he has been drooling and seems to prefer sitting upright.
